v.why: Raising an already large learning rate (0.0774 and above) causes unstable or divergent Adam training, while raising it elsewhere helps or is neutral.
At very small learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so raising the rate gives a large gain.
With a tiny learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and more undertraining, so increasing batch size hurts more.
Small batches combined with a high learning rate give noisy, unstable updates, so decreasing batch size hurts more.
Widening a narrow network adds capacity and helps, whereas gains saturate at large widths.
At large widths there is little capacity gain left, and wider nets are more prone to overfitting or instability, so the effect is lower than elsewhere.
Deeper ReLU nets are more fragile at high learning rates, so adding layers hurts more there.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty (0.129 to 1) causes underfitting, unlike increases at small alpha, which do nothing.
Relaxing a very strong L2 penalty relieves underfitting, giving a larger gain than lowering alpha when it is already negligible.
Going from 1 to 2 layers adds more useful representational power than going from 2 to 3.
